title: Mulberry: Ancient Mulberries You Can Visit
meta_description: Three old mulberries nobody has named black or white. One in Lewes is put at more than 350 years; a reader dates a pollarded one near Milan to 400.
intro: Not one of these three mulberries has been named to species, so each is waiting for somebody to settle whether it is black or white. In Lewes, Southover Grange Gardens keep one that the Parks and Gardens record of the garden puts at more than 350 years. Its short, leaning trunk breaks into heavy limbs, several of which have come down to rest along the grass. In Taranta, a quarter of Cassano d'Adda east of Milan, a reader sent us a pollarded mulberry, its thick grey arms cut back the old way for their leaves, and puts it at 400 years. Lombardy once kept mulberries like this by the thousand to feed silkworms. On the Oberdorfplatz in Möhringen, the old village centre that is now a Stuttgart district, the city protected a third in June 2003 for its character, its rarity and its cultural significance, and never published an age or a girth. White mulberry leaves are glossy and black mulberry leaves are rough as sandpaper. If you can feel the difference, tell us on the tree's page.
